clue.text: Pets surrounding small boy companion with container appear in children's play

indicators.note: to surround something is to stand on all sides of it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: two pets, each a cat, split to go either side
Chas is the short form of the boy's name Charles
CH stands for Companion of Honour
a can is a container

explanation.surface: Children's pets and a small boy with his friend and a tin turn up in a nursery game.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas is the usual short form of Charles; the pets come as a pair so that they can sit either side of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Catch-as-catch-can is a free-for-all style of wrestling or rough game, using any hold or method available.

clue.text: Swallow eccentric female, German with German crime

parts.note: to swallow a story is to credit it, believe it
a card is an eccentric or comical person
Frau is the German word for a woman or wife
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A list of odd characters, an eccentric woman and a German, implicated together in some offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'German' qualifies the female, giving the German word for woman; the second is just a one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudulent use of someone's plastic payment card is an offence, an example of criminal deception.

clue.text: Prominent part of artist in chairman''s liqueur

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another is held within it, so the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese leader; the possessive is surface dressing
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; RA'S CHIN is a prominent feature of the face

explanation.surface: Some notable feature of a painter turns up in the chairman's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist's chin goes between MA and O of Mao, the famous Chairman.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a clear Italian cherry liqueur distilled from marasca cherries.

clue.text: Looks like an affectionate message

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gazes, as in regarding someone closely
second meaning: kind wishes sent at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Something has the appearance of a fond note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks like' reads as one phrase, but the verb stands alone as the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both gazes at and the friendly greetings sent at the close of a letter, as in 'give her my regards'.

clue.text: It forsakes preaching for fiction

indicators.note: to forsake is to abandon or leave, so these letters walk out of the longer word

parts.note: a preacher speaks from the raised platform in a church
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone abandons sermons in favour of writing stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The place of preaching, PULPIT, loses IT to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulp is cheap, sensational fiction, named after the low-grade paper of the old magazines.

clue.text: A Virago author (Jewish-American-Italian) in a line of very low degree

indicators.note: something placed inside another is enclosed by it, so the bracketed nationality sits within the line

parts.note: taken as written
a virago is a nagging, bad-tempered woman, a scold
Sholem Asch was a Jewish-American novelist
taken as written
RY is short for railway, a line
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: A writer published by Virago, of mixed ancestry, sits in a queue of very humble standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Virago is also a feminist publisher, which makes 'Virago author' look like one phrase; here a virago is a nagging woman. Sholem Asch wrote in Yiddish and settled in America.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As cold as charity' is an idiom for extremely chilly, so a temperature of very low degree.

clue.text: Kazan's one among many reforming weirdo: fat chance!

indicators.note: reforming means forming again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film director's odd man out is unlikely to change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia Kazan directed the 1957 film of this title, and the phrase also means one anonymous person among many.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an ordinary individual lost in a mass of people, and names Kazan's 1957 picture.

clue.text: Motion supported by gilded student

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
aureate means golden or gilded

explanation.surface: A proposal backed by a privileged student.
explanation.walkthrough: Motion is not a proposal but Andrew Motion, who was Poet Laureate when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Motion held the post of Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009, so he is an example.

clue.text: Involving risks before conviction

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a word that can stand before 'conviction' in a legal phrase

explanation.surface: Taking chances ahead of being found guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: An unsafe conviction is one a court of appeal can quash because doubt hangs over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means dangerous, and in British law describes a guilty verdict that cannot safely stand.

clue.text: Champion needs help when returning from torpor

parts.note: an ace is a champion, an expert

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for help is read from its end

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A champion needs assistance to come back from a sluggish state.
explanation.definitionFit: Acedia is spiritual sloth or listless apathy, one of the old deadly sins, hence a torpor.

clue.text: Come close at first very quietly to fish

indicators.note: the word at the front of the clue keeps only its opening letter, the one that comes first

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler creeps up silently on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to draw near, to get closer to something.

clue.text: Hypocritical words have no power

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the contraction of 'cannot', with its apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Insincere talk achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords ignore punctuation in answers, so the contraction of cannot counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is sanctimonious, insincere speech; the contraction means being unable, lacking ability to act.

clue.text: Rebel freed to rebel endlessly in mountain

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the second word for revolt is dropped

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
rid means freed, as in 'rid of'
to rise is to rebel, rise up

explanation.surface: A rebel let loose to stir up revolt again in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb meaning revolt loses its final letter. Cader Idris is a mountain in Snowdonia, North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cader Idris is a peak in the south of Snowdonia National Park, Wales.

clue.text: Christmas dinner in the oven: go in, flower girl!

indicators.note: telling something to go in means it enters and sits inside the following name

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name and a flower
an oast is a kiln, an oven for drying hops
taken as written

explanation.surface: The festive bird is cooking, and a bridesmaid is told to go into the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' suggests a wedding, but it is the girl named after a flower. The hop-drying kiln and GO go inside her name after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked goose was the traditional English festive meal before turkey took over.

clue.text: Fight that is a problem for sheep

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A brawl that causes trouble among the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for 'that is' needs both clue words, so 'is' does double duty only in the surface: here 'that' gives the letters and 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal degenerative brain disease of sheep and goats.

clue.text: Unnatural condition for lift, say

parts.note: surface reading: a medical or mechanical state that is abnormal for an elevator
setter's reading: a cosmetic lift, such as a facelift or padded bra, creates a false appearance

explanation.surface: An elevator is behaving abnormally.
explanation.walkthrough: A facelift or a padded bra gives an artificial lift, so falseness is the condition it creates.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsity is the state of being untrue or not genuine, which is what an artificial lift produces.

clue.text: Greek vase featuring Doctor Love is worth little

indicators.note: a vessel featuring decoration has it within its body, so the vase holds the other pieces

parts.note: an olpe is an ancient Greek jug
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An ancient pot showing a doctor and love has little value.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor and love go together inside the Greek jug. 'Money for old rope' means money for something worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Old rope stands for something valueless, as in the idiom 'money for old rope', easy money for trash.

clue.text: Way to rebellion of California model in single room

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
UDI, Unilateral Declaration of Independence, as declared by Rhodesia in 1965
taken as written
LA, Los Angeles, the California city
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A route to revolt by a Californian fashion model who lives in one room.
explanation.walkthrough: California here stands for its best-known city. UDI was Rhodesia's breakaway from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a small apartment with one main room for living and sleeping.

clue.text: Male journalist gives notice

parts.note: the male pronoun
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaperman hands in his resignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives notice' looks like resigning, but 'notice' is the noun meaning attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Heed is attention or regard, as in 'take heed', the same as notice.

clue.text: Shakespeare's friend back to venerate in any other place?

parts.note: Mr W.H. is the mysterious dedicatee of Shakespeare's Sonnets

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the verb for honour is read right to left

parts.note: to revere is to venerate

explanation.surface: A friend of Shakespeare returns to honour him, wondering where else he could be.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'only begetter' of the Sonnets is named only by the initials W.H.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherever can mean in any place at all, or, as an emphatic question, where on earth.

clue.text: The wind indicator sounds useless

indicators.note: sounds says the answer is heard like another word, spelt differently

parts.note: in vain means to no purpose, useless

explanation.surface: A weathercock that seems to serve no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather vane turns on a rooftop to show which way the wind is blowing.

clue.text: Astronomical model or engineers on line

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A model of the heavens, or engineers working on a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system showing the planets orbiting the sun.

clue.text: South American entertainment seen in the foregoing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
A is short for American
a turn is a performer's act or entertainment

explanation.surface: A South American show featured in what came before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one description, but it splits into two abbreviations. The foregoing is the previous answer, the solar system model.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a planet, so it appears in an orrery, the model of the solar system clued just before.

clue.text: After time, have part of address

parts.note: post is the Latin-derived prefix meaning after
T is the abbreviation for time
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Later on, one is given a share of the speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech, but it is a postal address.
explanation.definitionFit: In British postal addresses, the post town is the line naming the town of the sorting office.
